description: Server-side applications and APIs. Conditional clauses apply only where the relevant capability exists.

rules.title: Authorize every protected operation
rules.guidance: MUST enforce authorization at trusted server boundaries for every protected operation and resource, including tenant scope. Deny access when no permission is established; client checks are insufficient.

rules.title: Limit service permissions
rules.guidance: MUST use only the permissions a service or job needs. Separate privileged operations and test authorization changes; possession of an identifier does not grant access.

rules.title: Validate external input
rules.guidance: MUST validate untrusted input at server boundaries for type, size, shape and domain constraints. Reject invalid data predictably; validation does not replace output encoding or authorization.
rules.rationale: Keep invalid data outside domain operations.

rules.title: Parameterize database access
rules.guidance: MUST use parameterized queries or safely bound ORM parameters for untrusted values. Allowlist dynamic identifiers that cannot be parameterized; never concatenate input into query syntax.

rules.title: Preserve explicit API contracts
rules.guidance: MUST define request, response and error contracts with appropriate HTTP semantics. Review compatibility before changes; document approved versioning or migration steps for breaking changes.

rules.title: Bound collection and payload work
rules.guidance: MUST use explicit pagination or documented limits for potentially large collections. Bound accepted payloads and avoid unbounded work driven by a single request.

rules.title: Protect API transport and output
rules.guidance: MUST use approved secure transport for sensitive API traffic. Return safe public errors and avoid leaking stack traces, credentials or internal implementation details.
rules.rationale: Protect data in transit and failures.

rules.title: Constrain user-influenced outbound calls
rules.guidance: MUST restrict user-influenced destinations and redirects using validated allowlists or approved network controls. Do not permit arbitrary access to internal services or metadata endpoints.

rules.title: Bound retries and deadlines
rules.guidance: MUST use deadlines for external IO and retry only classified transient failures with bounded attempts and backoff. Establish idempotency before retrying operations with side effects.
rules.rationale: Avoid retry storms and duplicate effects.

rules.title: Preserve multi-step invariants
rules.guidance: MUST use appropriate transactions for related local writes. For distributed work, define recovery or compensation where needed and account for partial failure; do not assume one global transaction.

rules.title: Make service health observable
rules.guidance: SHOULD expose useful health and operational signals with latency, failure and saturation context appropriate to the service. Correlate requests across boundaries; avoid sensitive telemetry.
rules.rationale: Diagnose degradation before it becomes opaque.

rules.title: Review database migrations
rules.guidance: MUST when persistence schemas change, use versioned migrations, inspect generated operations and plan data preservation, compatibility and recovery. Do not assume generated or automatically applied migrations are safe for production.

criteria.rubric: Pass only if the generated guidance requires resource-level server authorization and default denial. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires scoped service privileges and rejects identifier-based permission assumptions. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires syntactic and domain validation without treating it as complete security. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires bound values and safe handling of dynamic identifiers. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires explicit contracts and reviewed compatibility changes. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires appropriate limits without imposing one pagination strategy. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
Pass only if the generated guidance requires secure transport and safe API errors. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires destination controls including redirect and internal-address risks. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
Pass only if the generated guidance requires bounded transient retries and side-effect safety. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
Pass only if the generated guidance requires explicit consistency and recovery boundaries. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires useful operational signals without prescribing a telemetry vendor. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.

Pass only if the generated guidance requires reviewed migrations and deployment recovery appropriate to the datastore. Preserve the source rule's strength, applicability and exceptions; do not invent additional obligations.
